text:
Maya (People Ops): Quick Q — international dental office in Madrid is asking if Redwood can direct-bill for a root canal. They want EFT assignment + an EOB with PHI redacted before sending to the patient. Provider attached a scanned claim form and says they bill in EUR. Claim ref: 2026-INT-8421. Who owns the provider EFT flow and what docs do we need?

Liam (Benefits): We do allow direct-bill for major procedures but several checks first. Need provider tax docs, a signed Assignment of Benefits (AOB), and a bank remit form for international EFT.

Jess (Finance): Also need provider NPI (or local equivalent) and a copy of the provider's banking instructions with IBAN/SWIFT. For redaction: we can remove SSN, full DOB, and patient address on the EOB PDF on our side, but we need the patient-signed consent to redact and for assignment.

Maya (People Ops): Got it. The clinic wants a template we can send them (they're asking for "what to fill out"). Can someone paste a short provider-facing template we can forward?

Liam (Benefits): Here — short email + required attachments:

```
To: billing@clinic.es
Subject: Redwood Inference — Direct Billing Request for member [MemberName]

Hello,

Thanks for offering to direct-bill. Please provide the following so we can process payment via international transfer:

1) Signed Assignment of Benefits (AOB) from the patient (scanned PDF)
2) Provider banking details (IBAN, SWIFT/BIC, account name)
3) Provider tax registration or equivalent (scanned)
4) Clinic billing form / itemized invoice (in EUR)
5) Provider remit contact name + billing email/phone

Send all items to claims@redwood.com and reference Claim 2026-INT-8421. We will review and confirm estimated processing time.

Best,
Redwood Claims Team
```

Jess (Finance): Add: "Please indicate if you accept payment in USD instead of EUR and provide remittance instructions for USD if available." That avoids FX delays.

Maya (People Ops): Perfect — I'll forward. One more: provider asked whether we can "redact everything except CPT and amounts" on the EOB before sending to member. Is that allowed?

Liam (Benefits): We can redact certain identifiers (SSN, exact DOB, patient address) but we must keep service dates and charges for audit trails. CPT codes usually stay. Also the member needs to sign consent for redaction + assignment.

BenefitsBot: Automated: International claims flagged for manual review — expected adjudication 5-10 business days after all docs received. You will get a confirmation thread when payment is scheduled.

Jess (Finance): Timeline note: once docs are good, finance needs 3 business days to validate banking, then 5-7 business days for international transfer depending on the bank.

Maya (People Ops): Thanks all. I'll send the template and request the AOB + consent. Will update here when provider replies (cc: claims@redwood.com). :thumbsup:

Liam (Benefits): If provider pushes back on the AOB wording, send them this short consent language to include in the patient-signed doc: "I assign payment for services to the provider and authorize Redwood Inference to send a redacted EOB to me as described above."

Maya (People Ops): Copying that in. End of thread for now.
